correctness.rationale: For n≥2 no vertex dominates alone. An independent dominating union must use exactly one endpoint of each private pair. The chosen coalition's two supports partition the base indices; the remaining blocks' nonempty supports partition the same indices a second time. If at least three residual blocks remain, none can partner another residual block, yet at most two can have supports complementary to the original two blocks. A sole residual block would have full support and no partner. Thus there are exactly four blocks with two copies of each complementary support, and their 2-by-2 coalition graph without isolates has a perfect matching. Its unions give a proper 2-coloring, and conversely splitting either side of such a coloring into two nonempty blocks gives coalitions. The 2^(c−1)(2^(n−1)−1)² unordered-coloring presentations double-count exactly the partitions for which switching the matching flips colors on a union of components: a crossing base edge would become monochromatic, while without such an edge the switch works. Each of the 2^(c−1)−1 component splits gives 2^(c−2) doubly presented partitions when c≥2; there is no correction when c=1. The K₂ singleton partition is the only n=1 case. The finite recorded checks are consistent with these arguments.

evidence: Proposition 4.8 supplies the structural bipartiteness implication in the four-block case. Proposition 6 of the later paper bounds the coalition graph of a minimum-degree-one graph by K_(2,k−2), for a k-block independent partition; its case results concern extremal numbers, paths and cycles. The catalogue ordinary result proves C(G∘K₁)=4.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Every independent coalition partition is an ordinary coalition partition, hence the known ordinary bound already implies at most four blocks. The minimum-degree-one incidence bound alone does not count the valid independent partitions or resolve alternate perfect matchings.

evidence: Ordinary domination needs a hit in each private pair; independence additionally requires exactly one endpoint and forbids simultaneous selection of adjacent roots. The second matching survives precisely across a split with no crossing core edge.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The upper bound and the bipartiteness implication overlap structurally with known work. Neither they nor the connected-tree specialization give the component-dependent multiplicity of independent color-and-split presentations, which requires a new constraint on the partner matchings.

evidence: A four-block independent partition here encodes a split of a two-part idomatic partition, also called a fall 2-coloring. The closest catalogue record on leaf-corona pair incidence instead permits dominating unions regardless of independence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Unlabelled blocks are not orbits under automorphisms of the base. Counting split fall 2-colorings requires taking the image rather than counting presentations, and the ordinary problem omits the root-edge restrictions on that image.

originality.rationale: Credit is for the exact independent-partition enumerator on arbitrary bases, especially the disconnected presentation correction and coverage beyond trees. An ordinary-coalition upper bound, the broader four-block bipartiteness implication, and the reported connected-tree count are not credited as distinct contributions.
residual_risks: The 2026 counting preprint's broader coverage was not independently checked because its full text was not retrieved; the bounded literature and catalogue search does not certify priority.

value.rationale: The partition polynomial distinguishes bipartite from nonbipartite arbitrary bases and reveals an exact edge-independent count within each bipartite (n,c) class, despite independence being edge-sensitive. The correction quantifies exactly when different proper colorings produce the same unlabelled partition; it is needed even for elementary disconnected examples and is not supplied by a maximum-size result.
